# Priors
This thread introduces the central question: Can we construct a functorial theory of prior specification, comparison, combination, realization, and compilation into trainable architectures?

We want to treat inductive priors as mathematical objects independently of the architectures realizing them because we want to study the relations between priors and architectures, and priors and generalization, more explicitly.

There appears to be a broad and empirically important class of structural priors whose common mathematical invariant is naturality with respect to a category of transformations, relations, or contexts. What is the appropriate category of such prior specifications, how does each specification determine a class of admissible models and architectures, and how do these restrictions affect learning dynamics and generalization?
